account: Today appears quiet from what I have actually seen and heard, though I still have a feeling that town business may be happening without my knowing. Several townsfolk independently repeated that the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. The neighbour said the baker is making fresh bread for today's market. That is consistent with ordinary baking, and I have no evidence of another purpose. I tried to approach freight for independent news, but freight had already left my view, so I learned nothing from that lead. The secretary reports no correspondence, financial figures, expenses, or requests submitted today. I read my appointment book and a separate briefing and returned both to the appointments chest. I asked the secretary to prepare an accounts summary and record public meetings or unusual news; I have not yet received that summary. The neighbour confirmed our usual three o'clock tea at the east-bank dockside cottage, specifically (16, -60, 105). I have arrived early, at about 14:31, and can see the neighbour waiting by the open door. My next scheduled office visit is 16:30, and tomorrow's schedule includes a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill. So far, there is no confirmed unusual gathering or hidden activity, and no sound basis for accusing anyone. Tea offers a natural opportunity to hear more about life on the east bank.
